guides.h1: How to Watermark a PDF Free — Text or Logo
intro: A watermark tells readers what a document is before they open it: draft, confidential, sample, or a reminder of who owns the copy. It also makes casual reuse and screenshotting less attractive.

intro: Redaction failures have leaked medical records, court filings and personal addresses because someone drew a black rectangle over text and called it done. In many PDFs the text underneath is still there, selectable and searchable.

In Redact PDF you place black boxes on the pages that need them. On Run, each affected page is rendered at high resolution, the boxes are painted into the bitmap, and that image becomes the new page. The original page content — text, vector data and hidden objects — is not copied into the output.

Are formulas and formatting preserved?
Values are extracted into a simple table; formulas, colours, merged cells and conditional formatting are simplified. Use Excel's own print-to-PDF for presentation-perfect sheets.
Why is my wide sheet cut off?
PDF pages are fixed width. Reduce columns, use landscape print settings in Excel, or split the sheet into logical tables before converting.
Can I convert a CSV file?
Yes. Comma-separated files are parsed into rows and columns, with the first row treated as the header.
Is my spreadsheet uploaded?
No. Parsing and PDF generation happen entirely in your browser.
guides.h1: How to Convert Excel to PDF Free (XLSX & CSV)
intro: Spreadsheets are excellent working tools and awkward shared documents: column widths shift, formulas recalculate, and the recipient may not have the same software. A PDF freezes the table for review.
This guide explains what the browser converter does with XLSX and CSV files, where its simplified output is appropriate, and when to use Excel's own print-to-PDF instead.

body: The converter reads the first worksheet, extracts displayed values, and lays them out as a PDF table with a header row. CSV files follow the same path, with the first row becoming the header.
This is ideal for price lists, simple inventories, schedules, budgets and data extracts that need to be reviewed or attached to an email — not for reproducing a fully designed financial model.
sections.h2: From spreadsheet rows to a readable table

body: Formulas are replaced by their values, because a PDF should show the result rather than a live calculation. Colours, merged cells, charts, images and conditional formatting are not reconstructed. Very wide sheets can run past the page width.
For a board pack or a customer-facing report, use Excel's Print → Save as PDF with a defined print area and page breaks. The browser tool is the fast, private option for content-first tables.
Move the relevant data to the first worksheet, delete empty columns, and shorten verbose headers. If the table is too wide, split it into two logical tables or transpose the layout in Excel first.
Add a title in the tool's Title field so the PDF has context when it is forwarded. For a multi-document submission, merge the resulting table with a cover letter or report afterwards.
Workbook parsing uses SheetJS in the browser, and the PDF is generated locally. Financial data, staff lists and client records never leave the device.
Keep the source workbook as the editable master. The PDF is a snapshot, not a replacement for the file that contains formulas and source data.

steps: Open Excel to PDF and add an .xlsx or .csv file
Move the target data to the first worksheet before uploading
Set a title for the PDF and click Run
Review the table, then download and share
Use Excel's print-to-PDF when exact formatting is required
tips: Delete empty columns and shorten headers before converting.
Split very wide tables into two logical PDFs rather than shrinking the text.
Keep the workbook as the editable master; treat the PDF as a snapshot.

guides.description: Fill fillable PDF forms in your browser — text fields, checkboxes and dropdowns. Optionally flatten to lock the answers. No upload or signup.
faqs: What if the PDF has no fillable fields?

The tool needs an AcroForm PDF with real form fields. If the form is a flat scan or an XFA form, it cannot fill it — use Annotate or Create PDF to overlay text, or ask the issuer for a fillable version.
Should I flatten after filling?
Flatten when the answers should be final and non-editable, which is the safe default for submissions. Keep fields editable only when the recipient must revise them.
Are radio buttons and signature fields supported?
Text fields, checkboxes and dropdowns are supported. Radio groups, signature fields and unusual XFA controls may be left untouched.
Does filling a form change the original?
No. The tool produces a new PDF with your values; the source file is not modified.
Is my form data uploaded?
No. Fields are read and filled locally with pdf-lib; answers never leave the browser.
guides.h1: How to Fill a PDF Form Free (Text, Checkboxes & Dropdowns)
intro: Fillable PDFs are supposed to remove printing and handwriting. In practice, broken viewers, tiny fields and accidental edits create a new set of problems — especially when a form must be submitted in one clean pass.
This guide shows how to fill AcroForm fields locally, lock the answers with flattening, and recognise when a PDF is not actually fillable.

body: A PDF can look like a form and contain no interactive fields at all. After upload, this tool lists the fields it detects: text boxes, checkboxes and dropdowns. If the list is empty, the document is flat or uses an unsupported form technology.

Scanned paper forms fall into the flat category. For those, use Annotate to place text boxes over the page, or ask the issuer for an accessible fillable version. Guessing at coordinates is faster than rebuilding the form from scratch.
sections.h2: Check that the form is really fillable

body: Enter values for the fields you need and leave anything optional blank. Review every page in the preview before running the tool; a missed checkbox is easier to catch now than after submission.

Keep “Lock fields after filling” enabled for forms you are sending to someone else. Flattening turns the answers into page content so they cannot be accidentally edited or cleared by a different viewer. Disable it only when the recipient must still change the values.

If text disappears or a field refuses input, the underlying field may use a font or control this tool cannot write; the PDF still opens, but that field remains unchanged. Radio buttons and signature fields are common examples.

For signatures, use Sign PDF after filling: it places a drawn, typed or uploaded signature precisely on the page. For official filings, check whether a certified digital signature is required — an image signature is not the same thing.
Forms often ask for addresses, ID numbers, medical details or salary information. Filling them in a browser tab keeps that data local; nothing is uploaded to a server or stored in an account.
After submitting, consider clearing the downloaded file from shared devices and running the Privacy Scanner if you need to check the document metadata before archiving it.
sections.h2: Privacy when forms contain personal data

steps: Open Fill PDF Forms and upload the document
Wait for the detected fields to appear
Enter text, tick checkboxes and choose dropdown values
Keep flatten enabled to lock the answers
Click Run, review the PDF, then download and submit
tips: Use the preview to review every page, not just the first field.
Flatten before submitting unless the recipient must edit the form.
For scanned paper forms, use Annotate instead of expecting fillable fields.

guides.description: Recover a damaged or unreadable PDF in your browser. The tool rebuilds broken indexes and salvages readable pages — free, local, no upload.
faqs: What kinds of damage can be repaired?
Broken cross-reference tables, truncated trailers and minor structural corruption are the best candidates. A file with missing page content or severe byte-level damage may not be recoverable.
Will every page survive?
Not necessarily. The repair process rebuilds the document page by page and skips pages that cannot be read, reporting what was lost. Always inspect the result before deleting the original.
Can it repair a password-protected PDF?
An encrypted file may fail before repair because its contents cannot be decoded without the password. Unlock it first if you know the password, then repair the working copy.
Does repair restore the original quality?
It preserves whatever page content is still readable. It does not recreate missing objects or improve the quality of scans.
Is the damaged file uploaded?
No. Repair runs locally with pdf-lib and qpdf WebAssembly; the file stays on your device.
guides.h1: How to Repair a Corrupt PDF Free (Recover Readable Pages)
intro: A PDF that will not open is not always a lost document. Often the pages are intact but the file's index, trailer or cross-reference table is damaged — the equivalent of a book with a broken table of contents.
This guide explains how the browser repair tool rebuilds that structure, when recovery is realistic, and how to avoid destroying the only copy of a damaged file.

body: Typical signs include “cannot open file”, a blank viewer, pages that stop halfway, or an error about a broken xref table. These often point to structural damage rather than missing page data, which is exactly what a rebuild can address.

A file that is zero bytes, was interrupted during download, or fails with an encryption error is a different problem. Re-download the original first; if the bytes are incomplete, no repair tool can invent the missing data.

The tool first tries a tolerant parse with pdf-lib. If that fails, it hands the bytes to qpdf compiled to WebAssembly, which can reconstruct a broken cross-reference table and trailer. The recovered document is then rebuilt page by page.
Pages that cannot be decoded are skipped and listed in the result warnings. This page-by-page salvage is deliberate: one corrupt page should not prevent the other 40 from being recovered.

Open the repaired PDF in a second viewer, scroll through every page, and check the page count against what you expected. Look for blank pages or missing images, then compare with the original if any copy still opens.
Keep the damaged original until the repaired version has been reviewed and backed up. If the file contains signatures or form fields, expect those structures to be simplified by the rebuild.
Download PDFs completely before opening them, avoid editing files directly on unreliable network drives, and keep versioned copies before running heavy operations such as redaction or compression.
If a file is too large to open, use Large File Split & Join or the streaming split path instead of forcing it through a normal viewer. Repair is a rescue tool, not a substitute for a reliable backup.

steps: Open Repair PDF and add the damaged file
Click Run and wait for the structural rebuild
Read the warnings for any skipped pages
Open the repaired PDF and check every page
Keep the original until the recovery is verified
tips: Re-download the file first if the original transfer was interrupted.
Unlock encrypted PDFs before attempting repair.
Never overwrite the only copy of a damaged document.
guides.title: Repair Corrupt PDF Free — Recover Readable Pages

guides.description: Compare two PDFs side by side with synced scrolling in your browser. Spot contract changes and revised clauses without uploading files.
faqs: Does it highlight every changed word?
No. The tool is a visual side-by-side reader with synced scrolling, not an automated text-diff engine. It makes changes easy to spot but still relies on your review.
What happens if the files have different page counts?
The viewer continues to the longer document. Pages that exist only in one file appear on that side, so missing sections are visible.
Can I compare scanned PDFs?
Yes, as images. You are comparing the rendered pages visually, so scanned and flat documents work without a text layer.
Can I download a comparison report?
No. Compare is an in-browser review tool with no output file; it is designed for checking versions before you sign or send them.
Are the files uploaded?
No. Both PDFs are rendered locally and the comparison never leaves the browser.
guides.h1: How to Compare Two PDFs Free (Side-by-Side Review)
intro: Contracts, policies and reports rarely change in one obvious place. Comparing two versions by opening them in separate windows makes it easy to miss a moved clause or a quietly edited number.
This guide shows how to review two PDFs side by side with synced scrolling, what the tool does not do, and a practical checklist for version review.

body: The Compare tool renders both PDFs as page images and places them in two columns. Scrolling one side moves the other by the same amount, so corresponding pages stay aligned while you read.

It does not parse words, highlight insertions, or produce a change report. That is a deliberate trade: scanned documents, complex layouts and signatures compare correctly because the tool never depends on a text layer.
sections.h2: A visual diff, not a text diff

body: Start with the page count and the first page of each file. Then walk through every page, watching for moved sections, changed dates, altered amounts and new exceptions. Pay particular attention to definitions, termination clauses and anything involving money or liability.

When a page differs, zoom in and read both sides rather than assuming the change is cosmetic. If the documents are long, split them into matching sections and compare one section at a time to keep concentration high.

Annotate the version you are reviewing with comments or highlights, then share the marked copy with the other party. If the difference is sensitive, redact the shared copy rather than sending the full document.
For document sets, merge the reviewed files into a single packet only after the comparison is complete. Keep both original versions in your records so the change history is auditable.
sections.h2: What to do when you find a difference

body: Both PDFs are rendered in the browser and never uploaded. That matters for employment contracts, legal drafts, medical reports and financial agreements that should not be sent to a third-party comparison service.
The tool works offline after the app has loaded, so you can review confidential files on a disconnected device.

steps: Open Compare PDFs and add exactly two files
Wait for both documents to render side by side
Scroll through the pair and review each page
Annotate or redact the working copy as needed
Keep both originals for your records
tips: Check the page count first; missing pages are the easiest change to miss.
Compare matching sections in long documents instead of rushing the whole file.
Use Annotate to record findings before sharing the reviewed copy.

guides.description: Crop white margins or scanner borders from a PDF. Set top, bottom, left and right trims per page range — free, local, and non-destructive.
faqs: Does cropping delete the hidden content?
No. Cropping changes the visible page box while the original content remains in the file. Use Redact PDF if content outside the crop must be permanently removed.
Can I crop only some pages?
Yes. Enter a page range such as 1-3, 5 and leave the field blank to apply the same margins to every page.
What units are the margins in?
Margins are percentages of each page's width or height, so the same values work across mixed page sizes and orientations.
Will cropping improve print quality?
It changes what is shown and printed, not the resolution of the remaining content. For smaller files, compress after cropping.
Is the original modified?
No. The tool writes a new PDF with adjusted CropBox and TrimBox values.
guides.h1: How to Crop a PDF Free (Margins, Borders & Scans)
intro: Scanned pages often carry black borders, oversized white margins or a strip of the next page. Cropping makes the document easier to read, smaller to print and cleaner in a submission portal.
This guide shows how to trim percentages from each side of a PDF, target only the pages that need it, and understand why cropping is not the same as redaction.

body: The crop tool asks for a percentage to remove from the top, bottom, left and right of each page. Percentages adapt to portrait, landscape and mixed-size documents, which is more reliable than entering fixed measurements for every page.
Start with small values such as 2–5% per side, preview the result, and increase only where the unwanted border is obvious. The tool refuses margins so large that almost nothing would remain.
The page field accepts ranges like 1-3, 5, so you can trim the scanned appendix without touching the clean cover letter. Leave it blank to apply the same crop to the whole document.
This matters for mixed files: a uniform crop that fixes a phone scan may cut text from a normally formatted page. Organize the pages first if the document needs both reordering and cropping.
sections.h2: Crop only the pages that need it

body: The tool sets the visible page box (CropBox and TrimBox). The content outside that box still exists in the PDF and may be recoverable with another viewer or by removing the crop.

If the hidden area contains an address, account number or other sensitive text, use Redact PDF instead. Redaction rasterizes the affected page and destroys the underlying content rather than simply hiding it.
Open the new PDF and check the first page of each cropped range. If the document is heading to a portal, compress it afterwards; cropping alone reduces visible area but not necessarily file size.
The operation runs locally and writes a new file, leaving the original untouched. Keep the original if you may need the full page later.

steps: Open Crop PDF and upload the document
Enter trim percentages for top, bottom, left and right
Optionally enter the pages to crop (blank = all)
Click Run to generate the cropped PDF
Review the page edges, then compress if needed
tips: Start small and preview before trimming aggressively.
Use page ranges to avoid cutting normally formatted pages.
Use Redact, not Crop, when hidden content must be destroyed.
guides.title: Crop a PDF Free — Margins & Scanned Borders (2026)

guides.description: Turn paper into a multi-page PDF with your phone camera. Capture pages, review them, and save locally — free, private, no account or upload.
faqs: Do I need a dedicated scanning app?
No. The browser asks for camera permission, captures each page, and assembles an A4 PDF locally. Photos can also be uploaded if the camera is unavailable.
Are the captured pages searchable?
Not automatically. Photos are images. Run the resulting PDF through OCR if you need selectable or searchable text.
What happens if I deny camera permission?
The tool explains that the camera is blocked and lets you add photos through the normal upload path instead.
Are my scans uploaded?
No. Camera captures are processed in the page and assembled with pdf-lib; the images never leave the device.
Can I scan many pages in one document?
Yes. Capture as many pages as you need before running the tool; each capture becomes one A4 page.
guides.h1: How to Scan Paper Documents to PDF Free (Phone Camera)
intro: A phone camera is the scanner most people already own. The hard part is turning a stack of captures into one straight, shareable PDF without sending private paperwork through a cloud scanning service.
This guide shows how to capture clean pages in the browser, what to do about lighting and angles, and how to make the result searchable.

body: Open Scan to PDF, allow camera access, and fill the frame with one page at a time. Keep the phone roughly parallel to the paper, use soft indirect light, and avoid casting your shadow over the text.
Each capture becomes a page. You can scan receipts, signed forms, ID documents and handwritten notes in one session, then review the page count before generating the PDF.

The scanner fits each capture onto an A4 page with a small margin. That produces a predictable document for printing and for portals that expect A4, while preserving the whole photo rather than cropping it aggressively.
If a page is rotated or badly framed, retake it. The tool does not guess document edges or apply perspective correction, so a little care at capture time beats editing later.

The PDF is image-only until you run OCR. Upload it to OCR — Scan to Text, choose the document language, and let Tesseract.js add a text layer. The result keeps the page images and adds selectable text for search, copy and accessibility.
OCR accuracy depends on sharpness, contrast and language. For a contract or medical letter, proofread the extracted text before relying on it.
Camera frames are handled inside the browser and assembled locally. Nothing is uploaded, which makes the tool suitable for IDs, prescriptions, tax letters and other sensitive paperwork.
Photo-heavy PDFs can be large. Compress the finished file for email, and keep the original PDF as the archival copy. If the scan is one part of a larger application, merge it after compression.
sections.h2: Keep the scan private and manageable

steps: Open Scan to PDF and allow camera access
Capture one page at a time, filling the frame
Review the captures and retake any poor pages
Click Run to assemble an A4 PDF locally
Download, then OCR or compress as needed
tips: Use indirect daylight; direct overhead light creates glare on glossy paper.
Retake rotated pages instead of hoping the PDF will fix them.
Run OCR after scanning if you need to search or copy the text.

guides.description: Extract selectable text from a PDF as plain text or Markdown in your browser. Scans need OCR first. Free, private, no upload.
faqs: Why is the extracted text empty?
The PDF probably contains only page images, such as a scan or a photo export. Run OCR first to add a text layer, then extract the text.
Does it preserve tables and columns?
Plain text keeps reading order with page markers; Markdown adds headings and list structure. Complex tables and multi-column layouts may not match the visual arrangement exactly.
What is the difference between TXT and Markdown?
TXT is unformatted text suitable for notes and search. Markdown keeps headings and bullet structure, which is useful for documentation, wikis and content migration.
Can I extract text from a password-protected PDF?
Unlock the PDF first with Unlock PDF, then extract the text from the working copy.
Is the document uploaded?
No. Text is extracted locally with pdf.js and the output is generated in your browser.
guides.h1: How to Extract Text from a PDF Free (TXT or Markdown)
intro: PDFs are good at preserving appearance and bad at giving words back. Copying from a viewer often drags in line breaks, headers and page numbers; extracting the text layer produces a cleaner starting point.
This guide shows how to pull selectable text into TXT or Markdown, understand its limits, and add OCR when the PDF is only pictures.

body: The tool reads the text layer embedded in the PDF. Digital documents from Word, Google Docs, LaTeX and most publishing pipelines have one; scans and photos usually do not. If extraction returns nothing, the PDF is image-only rather than protected.

Page markers are inserted between pages so you can trace a quote back to its source. The extractor does not reconstruct images, charts or the visual position of every block — it returns the words in reading order.
sections.h2: What the extractor can and cannot read

body: Plain text is the safest output for search, notes, translation tools and scripts. Markdown is better when headings and lists should survive into documentation, a wiki or a CMS: the extractor maps styled lines to heading levels and bullets where it can.
Neither format recreates tables perfectly. If the data is tabular, PDF to Excel is the better route; if you need an editable document, PDF to Word produces a .docx.

A scan has no text layer to extract. Run OCR — Scan to Text with the correct language, then extract the text from the searchable PDF it produces. OCR reads visible characters, so blur, skew and handwriting reduce accuracy.
For a mixed document, OCR the scanned pages and extract the digital pages separately, then combine the text. This avoids paying the OCR cost twice for pages that already contain clean text.

Extraction happens locally with pdf.js; the PDF and the extracted text stay in the browser. That makes the tool suitable for contracts, research papers and internal reports that should not be pasted into an online converter.
Before publishing extracted text, proofread for hyphenation, ligatures and broken line breaks. Keep the original PDF as the authoritative source.

steps: Open Extract Text and upload the PDF
Choose TXT for plain text or Markdown for structure
Click Run to read the embedded text layer
Review page markers and clean up line breaks
Use OCR first if the document is a scan
tips: If extraction is empty, the PDF is image-only — try OCR, not a different extractor.
Markdown is better for docs; TXT is better for scripts and translation.
Use PDF to Excel when the content is tabular.
